groups.decision: Separate cloud feature declaration, licensed-seat governance, all-user repository exceptions and enterprise delegation. Neither seat inventory alone nor repository ownership alone determines all policies.
Enterprise policies are evaluated first; retain explicit enable/disable/delegate choices, cloud-agent selected-organization exception, and separate default for directly enterprise-assigned users.

Usually least-restrictive within an enterprise and usually most-restrictive across enterprises are qualified summaries. Use per-policy organization rules; preserve Team-model billing organization, plan transition, enterprise-specific AI-credit usage and unspecified Spark exception instead of inventing merge semantics.

Metrics API, non-GitHub semantic indexing, public-code privacy and unlicensed-member code review use most-restrictive organization combination. Semantic indexing requires all organizations explicitly Enabled; Unconfigured means disabled. Metrics reference link is ghec-conditional.

Retain all fourteen individually extracted least-restrictive table policies, including web search, client/agent features, MCP and previews. Any enabled organization enables user access only within the policy's actual scope, enterprise constraints and supported surfaces.

Client policies are independently configured and table support is policy applicability, not equivalent functionality. Cloud-agent Internet access survives a nonapplicable web-search policy. Public-code agent support is annotate-only and cannot prove blocking, copyright clearance or network isolation.

Separate unconfigured GA feature and model defaults from explicit choices, preview status and effective target settings. Preserve the pin's staged model-active/feature-coming-soon text and October22 editorial expiry; neither supplies a runtime activation receipt.

Review enterprise owner/custom AI-control roles and organization granular roles separately. Audit policy and organization-enablement changes; observed drift, approved change and effective behavior remain distinct.
Enterprise/organization setting procedures remain separately reviewed dependencies; no link certifies a setting, rights or world coverage.
Editor preview features: IDEs only; other seven table surfaces not supported. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Web search: IDEs and GitHub Chat supported; cloud agent, third-party agents, CLI, app, review and Spark not supported. Not network isolation. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Custom model configuration: IDEs, CLI, app and GitHub Chat supported; cloud agent, third-party agents, review and Spark not supported. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Public-code suggestions: IDEs supported; cloud and third-party agents annotate-only; CLI, app, GitHub Chat, review and Spark not supported. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Copilot MCP servers: IDEs, cloud agent, third-party agents, CLI, app and review supported; GitHub Chat and Spark not supported. Separate GitHub MCP third-party-host governance still applies. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Registry-only MCP: IDEs, CLI and app supported; remaining five table surfaces not supported. MCP enablement is not registry-only restriction. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Content exclusion: IDEs, cloud agent, CLI, app, GitHub Chat and review supported; third-party agents and Spark not supported. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Model configuration: IDEs, cloud agent, third-party agents, CLI, app and GitHub Chat supported; review and Spark not supported. Distinct from custom-model configuration. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.

Copilot Memory: Cloud agent, third-party agents, CLI and review supported; IDEs, app, GitHub Chat and Spark not supported. These are pinned applicability declarations, not actual settings or native behavior.
Business/Enterprise cloud scope and separate default-policy reusable are not actual target entitlements.

The pin supplies October22,2026 activation for configurable/not-yet-active feature defaults and impact-count banner; enabled-by-default is a scheduled source assertion, not live runtime proof. Preserve explicit configuration before activation.
Distinguish new GA, preview-to-GA transition and existing Unconfigured GA features; explicit settings do not silently become delegated defaults.
Enterprise Unconfigured and organization delegated-but-unconfigured states are distinct; no generic default rule supersedes explicit upstream choice.

Exclude previews, residency/FedRAMP restrictive model policies and cloud session storage. Feature scope includes Features & clients plus code review and Copilot MCP pages; UI grouping is not a universal feature set.

Model-default delegation differs from feature-default activation. Pre-GA, open-weight, retention-excluded Fable and nonconforming residency/FedRAMP models stay disabled by default; explicit scoped manual enablement is a different approved workflow. Default choice does not clear retention or model rights.
An applicable enterprise/organization can disable default enablement or individually disable a feature/model; procedure does not authorize or verify a change.
Feature/model settings and release monitoring remain independently reviewed dependencies; release awareness is not effective policy.

Declared enterprise-owner role, plan scope, licensed seats and delegation must be reconciled with concept-level custom permissions and effective enterprise constraints. A generic navigation GHES branch does not widen the cloud article scope.

Retain target selection, AI controls and distinct Agents/Copilot/Features & clients/MCP pages. Dropdown, toggle and named-policy configurations are procedures, not approved writes or behavior receipts. No immediate control does not imply no policy.
The reused MCP note preserves GA-only scope and third-party-host GitHub MCP exclusion; enterprise navigation does not erase this boundary.

Business users' described Allowed default and Privacy route require actual effective-setting review. Public-code availability does not grant output license or blocking assurance on annotate-only surfaces.
Feedback opt-in requires GitHub.com feature enablement and remains separate from AI-training consent or provider data-retention agreement.
First-time adoption guidance and reviewed conflict/surface references supply context only; no live setting or approval is certified.

Retain enterprise-wide baseline, organization delegation/targeted rules and opt-in preview team mode as different policy mechanisms. Generic owner metadata/navigation never verifies target permissions.

Unconfigured delegated models follow the applicable default policy; targeted organization rule precedence beyond the procedure remains unresolved, not inferred from global least/most-restrictive rules.
Enterprise Disabled bounds all grants; enterprise Enabled remains enabled. Team Optional is not deny. Multiple memberships union their grants; no team Disabled override exists in this procedure.

Prepared team settings are inactive before opt-in; organization-delegated access can regress during migration. Preview rollback restores pre-opt-in enterprise state and loses subsequent policy changes. Require approved before/after snapshots and behavior/recovery proof.

Default agent-app scope follows its installation organization/personal account; enterprise-team mode moves app model decisions to enterprise controls. App grants are distinct from team membership grants; partner app classification is not trust or authorization.
Model configuration navigation and surface references are source context, not an effective configuration or client enforcement receipt.
Keep capabilities, plans, policy, responsible-use and release monitoring as separate sources. A source recommendation to pilot does not approve a target or supply runtime evidence.
Assistive approval and agentic autonomy are descriptive source categories. Customization and provider support vary by surface; built-in protections are unverified until behavior-tested.
Invitation/eligibility/opt-in and preview change risk remain explicit. Website preview policy does not govern all surfaces. Many DPA-covered previews is not all previews or per-use rights clearance.

Utility models are automatic across plans/surfaces, hidden from user selection and cannot be individually disabled. Ordinary model deny, billing-line absence and premium-unit controls must not certify no processing; disabling Copilot entirely is the described exception.

Base applies to Business/Enterprise, supplies default when no models are enabled and has a documented 60-day automatic transition. Preserve announcement, client upgrade and enablement stages; pin dates are not current target proof.
One-year support runs from designation and describes availability, not frozen behavior, immutable pricing or independently verified contractual acceptance.
Separate Enterprise Cloud/residency eligibility, US FedRAMP precondition and listed model membership. Current overlapping US lists do not equate geographic residency permanently with certification.
Routing, authentication, processing and logs/storage claims are upstream assertions under enabled enforcement. Verify endpoints, client behavior and storage before effective compliance attestation.

Compatible clients and region deployment timing bound availability. General 2025+ heuristic is not an exact compatibility matrix; listed models can be utility-only. Future GA alternatives do not prove preview support.

FedRAMP and residency policies are distinct and disabled by default. Source pricing says ten percent extra credits for enforced requests; do not infer stacked surcharges, utility billing or authorize cost-bearing enablement.
Retain eleven pinned US model occurrences separately; membership is not independently certified or observed target allowance.
Retain twenty-one pinned EU variable identities separately; resolve names and version/feature/client availability before target or rendered-page certification.
